Attached is the subprocessor inventory (BlueOrbit_Subproc_List_v2.xlsx) and our proposed MSA redlines where we add the flow-down language we normally push for our downstream contractors (redlines_BlueOrbit_MSA_redlined.docx).

- Confirm whether Redwood requires an Order Form amendment for this subprocessor addition (we're flexible but want the contract to match operational reality).
- Provide the template subprocessor flow-down clause you expect (or confirm you'll accept our redline in the attachment).

We aim to onboard DataStream in the next 3 weeks; appreciate a quick band-aid response and then we can schedule a short sync to walk through audit, access, and retention windows.

Thanks,
Liam Turner
Head of Cloud Ops, BlueOrbit

High level from our side: we typically accept third-party subprocessors for telemetry where the vendor signs an excerpted flow-down (DPA annex) and we capture the subprocessor in our registry. Order Form changes are not always required for purely operational subprocessors unless the scope or SLA changes. That said, we need legal sign-off on your redlines and procurement to confirm audit/access wording.

Kimberly / Markus / Karthik — can you review the attached redlines and the inventory and advise whether:
1) We require an Order Form amendment to add DataStream (yes/no),
2) Whether the vendor redline is materially acceptable or we should provide our standard flow-down language, and
3) Any onboarding evidence we will require (SOC2 type II report, subproc questionnaire, or contractual attestation).

Subject: Re: Notice: addition of DataStream Analytics as subprocessor (logs ingestion)

Connor / team / BlueOrbit — thanks for the packet. I reviewed the redline and inventory. Summary of position and next steps: 

Summary (legal viewpoint):
- We will accept DataStream as a subprocessor for telemetry ingestion provided BlueOrbit obtains a written flow-down from DataStream that matches key DPA obligations (confidentiality, limited purpose, deletion timelines, breach notification, and no independent rights to use customer data).
- We cannot accept audit access language that creates an open-ended right for BlueOrbit's partners to access Redwood customer environments. We will accept a vendor-managed attestation + SOC2 Type II or equivalent for DataStream for the first 12 months.
- Order Form amendment: NOT required at this time because the contractual scope and pricing are unchanged. However, we need a signed DPA addendum (subproc annex) to be attached to the MSA and stored in our registry.

Action items (what we need from BlueOrbit):
1) BlueOrbit obtains DataStream's completed subprocessor questionnaire and the latest SOC2 Type II (or equivalent) report. If SOC2 is unavailable, an SSAE/ISO report + a security attestation will do, but we'll treat onboarding as conditional until evidence is received.
2) BlueOrbit to countersign Redwood's standard subprocessor annex; I've attached a tracked-redline version of your text with our required edits (see attachment redlines_BlueOrbit_MSA_redlined.docx).
3) Confirm retention windows in writing (DataStream must delete logs within 30 days unless explicitly agreed otherwise and documented in the Order Form).

Attachments referenced in-line: redlines_BlueOrbit_MSA_redlined.docx (contains our tracked changes and the subprocessor annex template).

Once BlueOrbit provides the evidence, Procurement (Markus/Karthik) and Legal will complete intake and sign-off; we should be able to turn this in ~4–6 business days from receiving materials.

Kimberly Park
Legal Ops, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Notice: addition of DataStream Analytics as subprocessor (logs ingestion)

Nadia — appreciate the quick turnaround. To confirm Redwood's position: 30-day delete is our standard for telemetry retention tied to this product line; we can consider a 45-day pilot only if BlueOrbit and DataStream agree to the following mitigations for that period:
- DataStream provides SOC2 Type II (or equivalent) and signs Redwood's subprocessor attestation before any data flows begin;
- BlueOrbit documents the pilot scope and end date and agrees in writing to transition to 30-day retention after pilot completion;
- No additional downstream sharing of Redwood-derived telemetry beyond DataStream without prior written consent.

If BlueOrbit can commit to the three mitigations above, Legal and Procurement will approve a 45-day pilot window for up to 60 days. Otherwise we need 30 days from day one.

Next steps: BlueOrbit to upload SOC2 + questionnaire and accept the attached subprocessor annex. Markus / Karthik — please confirm once intake item is created in ProcureTrack and add the DocuSign link to the HubSpot deal. Liam / Nadia — Connor and I propose a 30-minute sync Monday 09:30 PT to finish outstanding items; please confirm availability.
